title: perf-regression-investigation-playbook
body:
Purpose:
This working playbook is a lightweight, pragmatic guide for on-call and on-shift engineers to triage and investigate performance regressions in the serving runtime. It focuses on signal stitching, quick root-cause hypotheses, and an efficient bisect/canary comparison flow you can run in under 90 minutes for most regressions.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to production and pre-prod canaries (hosted + dedicated).
- Covers latency and throughput regressions, elevated error rate tied to perf, and sudden token-level cost spikes.
- Not a full postmortem — follow-up postmortems should use the postmortem template.

Quick intake (first 10 min):
1) Identify the alert class and scope:
   - Alert title + ticket (INF-xxxxx). Which route/model/batch size is affected?
   - Is this global, per-region, or single host? Check the alert tags and first 2 minutes of dashboard heatmap.
2) Snapshot the timelines (last 1h / 24h):
   - Latency: P50 / P95 / P99 token and request latency trends.
   - Throughput: requests/sec, tokens/sec.
   - Errors: 5xx rate and model-decoder failures.
   - Resource: GPU util, CPU steal, memory usage, network RPS.
3) Assign a signal owner and comms channel (Slack thread + ticket).

Signal taxonomy (what to look for quickly):
- Request-level latency spike (usually routing, queueing, batch formation issues).
- Tokenization or decoding stalls (long tail spikes in per-token time).
- KV cache misses causing repeated compute (seen as per-request compute time increase with low cache hit rate).
- Kernel regressions (GPU kernel time increase, often correlated with driver or runtime changes).
- Autoscaling / capacity exhaustion (queue length growth, pending requests).
- External dependencies (model fetch, weight-loading, KMS, metadata services).

Dashboard checklist (order to check):
- Global overview: combined latency heatmap (by region/model/route).
- Route breakdown: top 10 routes by increased p95 delta.
- Model variant view: compare current vs previous stable model variant.
- Batching histogram: distribution of batch sizes over time – look for reduction in batching efficiency.
- KV cache metrics: hit_rate, miss_rate, eviction_rate.
- Kernel/compilation metrics: kernel_time_ms, compile_count, kernel_error_count.
- GPU host metrics: GPU util, GPU temperature, GPU mem usage, nvml kernel stalls.
- Queue & backlog: request_queue_length, avg_wait_ms.
- Infra signals: node replacements, OOM kills, kube events.

PromQL / quick queries (copyable snippets we use often):
- P95 latency for route ABC: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(route_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/abc"}[5m])) by (le))
- Batch size histogram: histogram_quantile(0.9, sum(rate(batch_size_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses[5m])))
- GPU kernel time: sum(rate(gpu_kernel_time_ms_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(gpu_kernel_time_ms_count[5m]))

Rapid hypothesis checklist (10–30 min):
- Is the spike coincident with a deploy? Check deploy timelines and rollout IDs.
- Did model weights or quantization profile change? Compare model hashes and quantization tags.
- Are batch sizes shrinking (client-side change or routing)? Small batches can blow up token cost.
- Is KV cache hit-rate dropping? If yes, hypothesis: new prompts/prefixes or cache eviction policy change.
- Kernel/driver: are there driver updates or repros after last infra bootstrap?
- Autoscaler: any pod churn or node flapping?

Bisect and canary comparison recipe (recommended flow):
1) Canary vs stable snapshot comparison (15–30m):
   - Grab aligned test set of 50–200 synthetic requests representative of the failing traffic. Include short and long-seq examples.
   - Run them against stable (prev) variant and current canary with identical load pacing.
   - Capture per-request trace: queue_time, batch_wait, compute_time, kernel_time, kv_hit.
   - Compute per-request delta and rank by delta to find worst offenders.
2) Binary bisect (rollout / PR bisect):
   - If canary vs prev looks clean but production is bad, bisect recent PRs/deploys. Start with last infra/runtime commits (kernel/drivers/compilation flags).
   - Use 2-way split: reproduce on a single host/pool with toggles for suspect flags (e.g., enable/disable experimental kernel).
3) Parameter bisect (config changes):
   - Toggle batching window, queue thresholds, cache policies, quantization profile toggles. These are lower risk and can be A/Bed on a small % if infra supports it.

Evidence capture (what to save in the ticket):
- Time series screenshots (dashboard with zoom), top 20 delta requests from canary run, per-host flamegraph snippet or nvprof summary, and a short reproducible script used for the canary test.
- Attach logs: request traces (JSON), node-level dmesg/nvml logs if kernel suspected, kube events.

Common false-positives and gotchas:
- Sampling artifact: dashboards downsampled to 1m can hide short bursts. Re-query raw 5s data for final confirmation.
- Synthetic load differences: client pacing matters. A canary test must use the same arrival process.
- Model warm-starts: first few requests may be slower due to JIT or lazy kernels. Exclude warmup window.
- Cache churn from unrelated experiments (QA env hitting prod cache keys).

If you identify a likely root cause and need mitigation (first 30–60m):
- Rollback candidate: if a deploy caused regression, rollback the rollout and observe within 10m. Document rollback id and timeline.
- Fallback to variant: route traffic to compatible fallback model variant or quantization level.
- Temporary throttling: reduce concurrency or add rate-limits for the route to reduce queueing.
- Hotfix config toggles: adjust batching window or cache TTLs if safe.

Escalation matrix:
- If kernel/driver suspected -> page infra-ml oncall + release-eng (PGP).
- If model weights/quality suspected -> notify model-onboarding and applied-ml.
- If widespread cross-region -> SRE + infra to check control plane routing.

Post-incident capture (within 24h):
- Attach canary reproduction artifact and a minimal repro script into the ticket.
- Fill in timeline: detection -> owner assigned -> mitigations -> reason -> status.
- Add recommended follow-ups (root cause analysis, perf regression test in CI, alert tuning).

Open questions / follow-ups to improve this playbook:
- How often should we auto-run route-level canary diff jobs for early detection?
- Better tooling for automated per-token flamegraphs in the backend (low overhead).
- Standardize a 100-sample test corpus per service for quick bisects.

Appendix: quick checklist (one-line actionable items)
- Collect 1h/24h snapshots and assign owner.
- Run route-level P95/P99 comparisons and batch-size histograms.
- Do a small canary run with aligned inputs.
- Rank requests by delta and inspect top 10 traces.
- If deploy-linked, rollback and validate.
- Capture evidence and schedule RCA if needed.

Notes to self and heuristics: (messy workspace section)
- If cache hit drops but batch size steady, suspicious of new prompt prefixes or partial key mismatch.
- Kernel regressions usually show sustained kernel_time increase across models; if only one model affected, look at model-ops changes.
- For token-decode stalls, correlate with average generated length increases and decoder time percentiles.

History: created after repeated late-night regressions in August 2024 where bisect churn took too long. This consolidates heuristics we used across three incidents.
